title: Vali's Last Gift: the Golden Garland
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)

captions.instagram:
Vali wore a golden garland. And as he died, he gave it to the very brother he had driven out.

Vali wore a golden garland, a gift from his father Indra; Valmiki says it held his life, strength and splendour even after the arrow struck (Valmiki Ramayana 4.17.5). As he died, Vali told Sugriva: wear this divine golden garland (4.22.16). The brother he had driven out took it, and his joy turned to grief (4.22.17). Full 14-min video on our YouTube.

Did you know about Vali's golden garland?

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)

Verses:
• Rama said: "Lakshmana, uproot this flowering gajapushpi creeper and put it around Sugriva's neck." Lakshmana did. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.12.34-4.12.37
• Now notice this. Vali already wore a garland. A golden one, given by his father, Indra. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.11.37; 4.17.5
• But his life did not leave at once. Valmiki says the golden garland Indra gave him held on to his life, his strength and his splendour. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.17.4-4.17.5
• "Sugriva, fate never meant us to be happy together. This kingdom is yours now." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.22.4-4.22.5
• "Look at Angada, lying on the ground, full of tears. Now you must protect him." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.22.8-4.22.10
• "And Tara's judgement is never wrong. Whatever she says, do it." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.22.13-4.22.14
• "And Sugriva, wear this divine golden garland. Its splendour would leave it when I die." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.22.16
• That same golden garland. Indra's gift. The one that had held Vali's life until now. Now around Sugriva's neck. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.17.5; 4.22.18
• And Sugriva's joy turned to grief, like the moon in an eclipse. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.22.17
• "Angada, bear both joy and sorrow. Stay obedient to Sugriva." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.22.20-4.22.22
• And saying this, Vali gave up his life. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.22.24
